rationale: Small source-only research product closing two suspicions that would otherwise be re-investigated: the protocol-version gate cannot underflow because ProtocolVersion is a signed int (so the window the heartbeat fast path skips is real), and liveBootstrap cannot bootstrap a node with existing state because BootstrapCluster refuses on HasExistingState. The two new sources are S60 (config.go version constants) and S61 (api.go BootstrapCluster); no map change is proposed, so the accepted map stays at its current version and every accepted result keeps its basis.

feedback.answered: Two further entry-path suspicions were checked against source and closed rather than escalated. (1) The protocol-version gate looks as if it could underflow at the minimum: checkRPCHeader rejects when header.ProtocolVersion < r.config().ProtocolVersion-1 (raft.go:60-70), so a node configured at ProtocolVersionMin could in principle reject every peer. It cannot, because ProtocolVersion is a signed int rather than an unsigned type (config.go:99 with Min 0 and Max 3), so the expression evaluates to -1 at the minimum and no valid header is rejected. This also fixes the reading of the heartbeat finding: the gate that the fast path skips is a real, bounded window (-1 .. Max), not an accidentally impossible one. (2) liveBootstrap looked as though it could bootstrap a node that already has state, because it forces the current term to 1 and sets the last log from the bootstrap entry; it cannot, because BootstrapCluster refuses when HasExistingState reports state (api.go:252-259), and liveBootstrap is only reachable through the bootstrap channel on a node that has not been bootstrapped.
remaining: ReloadConfig notification scope remains a low-consequence lead: only a decreased HeartbeatTimeout signals the notify channels, so a decreased LeaderLeaseTimeout is not picked up until the current lease timer fires.

The processHeartbeat concurrency contract is an unresolved independent limit: its comment says main-thread only while the transport invokes it from a connection goroutine, and the fields it touches are individually protected.

Deployment-level premises of the four confirmed findings: real reachability of an unconfigured TimeoutNow sender, the election consequence of a fast-path heartbeat, whether batching FSMs are contractually exempt from ConfigurationStore, and how long a snapshot-installed tail persists under a live leader.
Still unread or partly read: observer plumbing, the file and in-memory snapshot stores, and net_transport beyond the heartbeat classification.
feedback.rationale: Both checks concerned existing records (the append-entries behavior and the heartbeat fast path) rather than adding new objects, so the map is unchanged and no map version is created. Recording the closures with their sources keeps a future turn from re-deriving them, and the protocol-version reading strengthens rather than weakens the heartbeat finding by confirming the skipped gate is a genuine window.
